articles.title: MARCH 2009
articles.summary: This document presents a calendar for March 2009, detailing daily observances and notable events, many of which are linked to educational activities and resources on NASA's 'The Space Place' website. It highlights a blend of general holidays, historical dates, astronomical phenomena like moon phases and the vernal equinox, and science-related topics for children.

articles.title: Saturn at opposition, and a couple more transits
articles.summary: This article details celestial events for March 2009, prominently featuring Saturn at opposition with opportunities to observe its rings and moon transits (Titan and Rhea). It also provides viewing information for Venus's inferior conjunction, a morning alignment of Mercury, Mars, and Jupiter, and the bright asteroid Ceres. Additionally, the piece includes an update on the Mars rover Spirit's temporary operational issue.

articles.title: Severe Space Weather
articles.summary: A NASA-funded study warns that severe space weather, like a "super solar flare" followed by an extreme geomagnetic storm, could cause widespread societal and economic disruption. Such an event would likely trigger cascading failures in the electric power grid, impacting essential services such as water distribution, food supply, communications, and transportation, with potential costs of trillions of dollars. The article emphasizes the need for resilient infrastructure and improved space weather forecasting to mitigate these serious threats, referencing the historic Carrington Event.

articles.title: Starry, Starry Night
articles.summary: This article details Barnard's Star, an M-class dwarf known for its exceptionally high proper motion, making its movement observable over years despite its dimness. Discovered by Edward Barnard in 1916, it is one of the closest stars to Earth and will eventually be the closest, notable for its magnetic variability and unique trajectory through the galactic halo. The document also briefly includes information on recent board elections and directions to a local park.

articles.title: The Last Month In Astronomy
articles.summary: This article compiles several recent astronomical updates from early 2009, covering new research suggesting a past 'flip' of the Moon and skepticism surrounding reported methane on Mars. It also highlights discoveries like the smallest exoplanet by COROT and 'rain' on Titan, alongside achievements by amateur astronomers. A multi-observatory image of M101 using Hubble, Chandra, and Spitzer telescopes is featured to celebrate the International Year of Astronomy.

articles.title: It Must Be Astronomical ...
articles.summary: This article, 'It Must Be Astronomical...', is a newsletter from the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) for March 2009. It features the club's telescope loaner program, provides recommendations for three deep-sky objects (NGC 2683, NGC 2509, N 2525), and lists several astronomical lectures and a star party scheduled from March to June. The document also includes club officer information, staff for the 'SJAA Ephemeris' newsletter, and various contact email addresses.
